viral_tweets.title_en:
Terence Tao on reading a hard proof with AI

"If you start with a much more complicated argument, I would not just one-shot the proof. That doesn't teach you much of anything."

"If there's a result which is true in all dimensions, ask the AI: can you simplify the argument to only do the one-dimensional case, and just remove all parts of the argument that don't have to do with high dimensions? You might get a simpler document that you try to understand first.?

"A lot of this you should be doing at a whiteboard or blackboard with pen and paper. These tools are useful for cleaning everything up, and if there is some nasty computation where you don't care to understand exactly how the signs work, you just need to know the answer, you can use these tools, but also knowing when not to use them is part of the challenge."

----
Full video on "SAIR" YouTube channel, (link in comment)

viral_tweets.title: Watching @LukeStephensTV react to the GTA 6 vibe coders has got me dying 😭 People who don't use these tools extensively on a daily basis are still very much underestimating them. As someone who's been vibe coding purely for fun every day for the past y
viral_tweets.title_en:
Watching @LukeStephensTV react to the GTA 6 vibe coders has got me dying 😭

People who don't use these tools extensively on a daily basis are still very much underestimating them. As someone who's been vibe coding purely for fun every day for the past year straight, here's my take on why these vague prompts actually end up working better than someone with technical know-how on the subject trying to write lengthy prompts.

AI has gotten so much smarter in every logical facet of computing that you need to just accept defeat and realize you're never going to outsmart it. You're not going to suggest something it doesn't know or come up with some novel solution it couldn't come up with itself. By trying to direct it in a certain direction, you end up poisoning your context to the point it'll tunnel vision on your idea, which may not be the most optimal solution. You have to let Claude take the wheel.

This is especially true for something like porting GTA 6 to PC. This is literally impossible for any human to do in anything less than months to years. There isn't a single human on the planet who truly understands all of the current recomp/translation layer projects we're seeing. It's moving so fast that if you took the time to fully learn how they're developed end to end, by the time you truly understand everything it's doing, the capabilities will have improved so much that they'll supersede your understanding once again.

Prompts are the new high-level language. Most programmers today never touch assembly, the same way assembly programmers stopped writing raw machine code. Each layer lets you stop worrying about the one underneath it.

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
我要求克劳德用来自美国的真实数据填充文明风格的游戏地图。 Opus 5.5 下载并解析了大量公共数据以及 7 小时和 45K 行代码……它可以工作了:)

- 31 个真实数据源，包括人口普查、BEA、BLS、EIA、NOAA、USGS、DoD、NPS、FAA、FEMA、CDC...
- 实际海拔、土地覆盖、GDP、就业、发电厂、矿山、港口、机场、基地、公园、大学、货运、灾害；所有这些都被协调到一个 25 公里的六角网格上。
- 数据被转换成文明语言，例如黄金收益率就是GDP。一个城市的地区是其真正的行业专业化：圣何塞有一个园区，底特律是“汽车城”。它的公民是真正的劳动力：圣何塞四分之一的工人是工程师、编码员或科学家，而全国只有四分之一。奇观是根据公布的规则来选择的，例如国家公园是根据游客数量来选择的，大学是根据研发支出来选择的，等等。
- 19 个镜头（收入、学位、信仰、灾难……）、524 条地铁的城市景观，以及 9 名顾问和 1 名探险家。 Explorer 将 3,100 多个县中任何一个县的任何列转换为链接到地图的表格和散点图。
- 克劳德决定跳过一些州和领地
- 使用 Claude Code 桌面应用程序、Opus 5.5 在介质上构建并打开超级代码。

它部署在这里：https://karpathy.ai/usaciv/ 和“？”也有源码链接。我不太清楚我要做什么，但浏览和玩起来真的很有趣。也许它可以扩展或内置到游戏中。我每周的克劳德引言只剩下一半了，所以其他人必须接替:D。克劳德还制作了预告片：
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://karpathy.ai/usaciv/ and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

而且通常是同一群人吹嘘他们的代理每天将 5 千万亿次提交直接推送到 prod，而无需审核。因为我们不再需要它们了
viral_ticker_tweets.author: @tobias_petry
viral_ticker_tweets.summary_zh:
你看到讽刺了吗？

同时，1Password 构建了一个架构，其中所有内容都位于您的计算机本地，并且它们被黑客攻击对您的秘密来说不是问题。这比其他人所做的更安全。他们几乎因此而获得荣誉？

再说一遍，我什么都不懂了。感觉越来越像艾精神病了。不再有批判性的思考，只有感受。
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
I don't understand my whole industry anymore. People are enraged that 1Password has been hacked and attackers had been able to deploy malicious code to backend services. Without a review.

And its often the same people who boast that their agents push five quadrillion commits each day directly to prod without review. Because we don't need them anymore. You see the irony?

At the same time 1Password build an architecture where everything is local on your machine and they've getting hacked is no issue to your secrets. Thats better security than everyone else is doing. And they barely get credit for that?

top_three.title: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
top_three.title_en: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
top_three.author: derstruct
top_three.content_snippet: HN 极客热议: 1 点赞, 0 讨论
top_three.summary_en: Neui has launched an integrated stack that combines a Go-based web framework (Doors) with an AI agent. By allowing developers to annotate UI elements, the agent can interact with the page, execute backend scripts, and automate workflows natively without the need for additional API layers or state synchronization.
paragraphs: Neui is an AI agent and a web framework built as one stack. The framework, Doors (Apache-2.0), lets Go teams build modern interactive apps with no separate frontend and no API layer. Neui adds the agent: it runs inside the user's session, sees the parts of the page you let it see, operates the UI like a user, and brings its own work environment for the jobs a chat alone cannot do.
Every feature you build for users is instantly usable by the agent, with a work environment powerful enough to automate the work your users do by hand.

Developers mark which parts of the page the agent may see and use, right in the existing markup. The agent then clicks, types and reads like a user, and the app's own logic runs. There is no per-action code to write and no state to mirror.

A tool is one Go function that runs on the server, with no endpoint or permission code to write. Developers decide what the agent can see and do right where they build the UI, so its access is scoped to each user and updates with the screen.

The agent gets its own file workspace, scripts that run bulk UI work in one step, spreadsheets, web search, MCP connectors, background tasks, and automatic handling of long conversations. One script can call every tool and work across the whole UI in a single step.

When a user needs functionality your UI doesn't have, the agent builds it on the spot, anything from a single screen to a specialized app. It runs in the page with the user's permissions, and the agent stays in the loop to make the decisions.
Your users get the chat experience they already know from chat apps, with nothing to build or purchase.

The conversation is prompt-cache friendly, so input costs an estimated 6 to 14 times less than in copilots that rebuild the prompt for every screen, depending on the provider's cache pricing. Built-in scripts do bulk work without extra model turns or context bloat.
The conversation, instructions and tools live on the server, and the browser sends only the user's new message. A tampered browser can't add tools, rewrite history or change what the agent is told.
Every open page runs on the server, integrated with the agent harness. You mark in the page template what the agent may see and use.
Works the real UI. The agent reads, fills and clicks the elements you mark, as the user would, and your handlers run as usual. There's no state to mirror and no action to re-implement.

~>neui.Use{ Desc: "Customer's email", // RW: the agent reads the value in the user's browser or writes its own. Rights: neui.RW, } <input type="email" name="email"> Tools in the template. Register agent tools right in the page template, based on the UI context and the user's permissions.

许多企业主、创始人和首席执行官现在需要与自己进行艰难的对话，他们的企业根本没有理由在这个新时代继续存在

linked_tweets.content_en:
A lot of business owners, founders and CEOs now need to have the difficult conversation with themselves that their business simply doesn't have a reason to exist anymore in this new era

I think the types of businesses (and people) that succeed in a post-AGI era might just be completely different

You understand better now the extremely aggressive pivots to AI many companies a few years ago did, completely resetting their company or rebuilding it from scratch after they realized this

I remember Replit for example was just an online IDE that you could use with other people (targeted to coders), it got big with coding teachers, then in 2024 @amasad hard pivoted it to be an AI app and site generator target to the opposite audience: non-coders, which caused lots of backlash, but that worked, now it's projected to hit $1B ARR by end of this year!

Anyway, we're in a completely new era with completely different dynamics for what businesses will survive and which will perish, what worked last year might not work this year anymore, and what works this year might not work next year anymore, because we're dealing with AI models that get exponentially better every year

news.title: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
news.title_en: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
news.author: derstruct
news.content_snippet: HN 极客热议: 1 点赞, 0 讨论
news.summary_en: Neui has launched an integrated stack that combines a Go-based web framework (Doors) with an AI agent. By allowing developers to annotate UI elements, the agent can interact with the page, execute backend scripts, and automate workflows natively without the need for additional API layers or state synchronization.
paragraphs: Neui is an AI agent and a web framework built as one stack. The framework, Doors (Apache-2.0), lets Go teams build modern interactive apps with no separate frontend and no API layer. Neui adds the agent: it runs inside the user's session, sees the parts of the page you let it see, operates the UI like a user, and brings its own work environment for the jobs a chat alone cannot do.
Every feature you build for users is instantly usable by the agent, with a work environment powerful enough to automate the work your users do by hand.

Developers mark which parts of the page the agent may see and use, right in the existing markup. The agent then clicks, types and reads like a user, and the app's own logic runs. There is no per-action code to write and no state to mirror.

A tool is one Go function that runs on the server, with no endpoint or permission code to write. Developers decide what the agent can see and do right where they build the UI, so its access is scoped to each user and updates with the screen.

The agent gets its own file workspace, scripts that run bulk UI work in one step, spreadsheets, web search, MCP connectors, background tasks, and automatic handling of long conversations. One script can call every tool and work across the whole UI in a single step.

When a user needs functionality your UI doesn't have, the agent builds it on the spot, anything from a single screen to a specialized app. It runs in the page with the user's permissions, and the agent stays in the loop to make the decisions.
Your users get the chat experience they already know from chat apps, with nothing to build or purchase.

The conversation is prompt-cache friendly, so input costs an estimated 6 to 14 times less than in copilots that rebuild the prompt for every screen, depending on the provider's cache pricing. Built-in scripts do bulk work without extra model turns or context bloat.
The conversation, instructions and tools live on the server, and the browser sends only the user's new message. A tampered browser can't add tools, rewrite history or change what the agent is told.
Every open page runs on the server, integrated with the agent harness. You mark in the page template what the agent may see and use.
Works the real UI. The agent reads, fills and clicks the elements you mark, as the user would, and your handlers run as usual. There's no state to mirror and no action to re-implement.

~>neui.Use{ Desc: "Customer's email", // RW: the agent reads the value in the user's browser or writes its own. Rights: neui.RW, } <input type="email" name="email"> Tools in the template. Register agent tools right in the page template, based on the UI context and the user's permissions.

news.content_snippet:
Avicena, a Sunnyvale startup that links AI chips with tiny LEDs instead of lasers, has raised more than $100M in Series C funding. It also has a new chief executive. Kevin Pope succeeds Marco Chisari and will lead the company as it brings its first product to market next year.

InterVest led the round, Avicena announced on Tuesday. Other investors include Tiger Global, Cerberus Capital Management, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund and AMD Ventures. Prosperity7 Ventures, Mitsubishi Chemica

The company's LightBundle platform utilizes MicroLED arrays instead of traditional lasers to address bandwidth and power bottlenecks in data movement between processors and memory in AI clusters.

paragraphs: Chinese AI companies Z.AI and Moonshot AI have to delay their next flagship models and are looking for new sources of training data. The effects now reach beyond previously known delays, after the US closed the cloud loophole for Nvidia chips, Nvidia halted shipments to Southeast Asia, and US companies cracked down on model distillation.

As a result, Z.AI's roughly 3-trillion-parameter GLM-5.5 model, planned for November, is likely to slip into the first quarter of 2027, Reuters reports, citing sources. To bridge the gap, the company released the 750-billion-parameter GLM-5.4 on Monday and says a new design lets it keep up with systems that have 2 to 3 trillion parameters. Without foreign computing power, Moonshot AI's development cycle could double from six to 12 months, likely delaying its next major model, Kimi K4, until mid-2027.

With OpenAI and Anthropic blocking data scraping for distillation, Moonshot is now turning to the latest models from Google and Meta for training and stepping up its search for compute capacity in Europe, according to the sources.

news.title: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
news.title_en: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
news.author: Stephanie Findlay
news.content_snippet: Incoming governor Gina Hinojosa pledged to rein in construction of new projects during her campaign — Hello and welcome to Energy Source, coming to you from Houston.
news.summary_en: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has resumed environmental permitting for data centers under a directive from outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott. The approvals include SpaceX's $24 billion gas-fired power and supercomputing complex near Brownsville, as developers scramble to secure rights before incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa takes office in January with a mandate to curtail industry expansion and tax incentives.
paragraphs: This article is an on-site version of our Energy Source newsletter. Premium subscribers can sign up here to get the newsletter delivered every Tuesday and Thursday. Standard subscribers can upgrade to Premium here, or explore all FT newsletters
Hello and welcome to Energy Source, coming to you from Houston.
Just as many suspected, Texas’s data centre freeze did not last long. Last week, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality resumed “the issuance of all permits related to data centre projects”.

TCEQ granted three air pollution permits for SpaceX’s $24bn Boca Chica gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility outside Brownsville, CloudBurst’s power plant near San Marcos and Atlas Energy Solutions’ facility north-east of Abilene.

TCEQ resumed issuing the permits after receiving a directive from outgoing Republican governor Greg Abbott’s office. The directive said the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, which manages the state’s electrical grid, had finished gathering information on how data centres affect local communities.

Data centre developers are rushing to get permits approved in the final weeks before the Texas Legislature meets in January under incoming Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa, who pledged to rein in data centre construction during her campaign.
Hinojosa said she would establish a moratorium on new development, end tax breaks for the industry and give local communities a greater say on the construction of new facilities.

Even before the midterm vote, Abbott had shifted from his pro-data centre pitch, issuing a wave of regulatory recommendations for the industry. Those included data centres paying their own way, bringing their own water and protecting the Texas grid.
The data centre boom has already slowed significantly as Ercot processes developer requests. In August, Ercot was considering more than 474 gigawatts of requests to connect to the grid.

But only 204 projects representing 66.4GW met the grid operator’s qualifications to be conditionally included as “base load”, meaning they will most likely be energised with their initial request, according to an Ercot update in September.

A further 158 projects worth 127.9GW met the qualifications to be conditionally included as “studied load”, meaning they may be given different allocations and wait longer to be connected to the grid. The Ercot interconnection study is only expected to start in April 2027 with no date set for completion, according to a lawyer familiar with the Ercot process.
Developers in Texas have already been choosing to build their own power centres to avoid delays, according to analysis by Cleanview, a market intelligence company that tracks data centre development.

news.title: UK plans strict rules for crypto DeFi sector
news.title_en: UK plans strict rules for crypto DeFi sector

inline_images.caption: The FCA says a stricter approach is needed to counter the chance of fraud, scams and money laundering © Chris Batson/Alamy
inline_images.alt: The FCA says a stricter approach is needed to counter the chance of fraud, scams and money launderin

news.author: Martin Arnold and Nikou Asgari
news.content_snippet: FCA points to Binance heist and ‘lack of consumer protections’ as reasons for tighter regulation of decentralised finance than in US and EU
news.summary_en: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), led by Jane Moore (Head of Payments and Digital Assets), plans to mandate authorization for DeFi platforms to close regulatory gaps in anti-money laundering and consumer protection. Regulators emphasize that the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack, where stolen assets flowed through DeFi protocols for laundering, necessitates stricter oversight beyond current market norms.
paragraphs: The UK financial regulator is planning to impose tight restrictions on the decentralised finance crypto sector, pointing to the recent $6.3bn heist at Binance as a reason to take a stricter approach than the US or EU to a sector that has long spurned government regulation.

The Financial Conduct Authority told the FT it planned to push ahead with requirements for so-called DeFi platforms to be authorised under its new rules. This would affect many blockchain-based services that are structured to have no controlling entity.

FCA officials said they were taking a deliberately strict approach to DeFi because of what they saw as a high risk of fraud, scams and money laundering and the limited ability of consumers to recover stolen assets or seek compensation.

DeFi platforms use automated smart contracts to execute trades or carry out borrowing and lending, rather than using traditional brokers or other intermediaries. Proponents value the sector’s independence from the financial mainstream and from government oversight.

Users of DeFi platforms typically hold their funds in their own self-custody wallets, rather than using custody services offered by centralised exchanges. Its advocates say DeFi provides a faster and better approach, but critics worry that the largely unregulated sector carries considerable risks.

The FCA pointed to last month’s record $6.3bn hack at centralised exchange Binance as a reason why DeFi platforms require regulation. As part of their efforts to launder the stolen money, the thieves moved vast amounts of tokens through DeFi exchanges, which do not freeze stolen assets, and converted them into other tokens to make them harder to trace.
“Recent hacks have underlined that operational resilience concerns are a challenge around DeFi,” said Jane Moore, head of department for payments and digital assets at the FCA.

“The speed and scale at which stolen funds move through DeFi platforms can frustrate attempts to freeze and block [their] transfer,” she said. “We are keen to see industry solutions to tackle this money laundering.”

Crypto executives say the UK’s position will put the country at a disadvantage by depriving British investors of innovative new products and services such as tokenised equities and crypto lending on decentralised platforms.

AAVE is the world’s biggest decentralised lending platform. Linda Jeng, chief legal and policy officer at AAVE Labs, a software company that builds products on the platform, has been lobbying the FCA to change its position, which Jeng called “highly problematic”.
“We’d be going down the wrong regulatory path; it’s about where along the technology stack it is appropriate to apply regulation,” she said.

Jeng has written to the FCA seeking clarification over what constitutes a “service provider” to DeFi platforms, and whether this includes companies engaged in activities such as providing fee information or sanctions screening. She argued that the FCA should not regulate activities that contribute to the security of decentralised platforms.

paragraphs: NETHERLANDS: The nationwide rollout of ERTMS in the Netherlands is proceeding too slowly, with the current pace risking a full transition only between 2060 and 2070, far beyond the original 2056 target. Now, the first steps towards a new approach to accelerate the rollout are proposed.

The Dutch ERTMS Programme Directorate describes the Dutch ERTMS rollout as ‘a major challenge for the coming decades’, and a challenge that has grown in its strategic analysis published on 9 April. It had become clear to the Directorate last year that the Netherlands is facing a “major challenge” regarding train safety, which poses a “threat to the continuity of the rail system” and was leading to rising costs for maintaining outdated systems.

To rise to this challenge, the Directorate is proposing a new approach, including an accelerated national rollout by 2040 and a shift from sequential to parallel installation across multiple regions. The ‘exploratory analysis’ examines the urgency and the possibilities for accelerating the roll-out of the ERTMS programme. The ERTMS Programme Directorate is an independent body within the rail sector that reports to the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management with input from all involved stakeholders.

The analysis points out three main reasons for the increasingly challenging ERTMS rollout. First of all, the Netherlands’ current ATB safety systems will reach the end of their lifespan between 2030 and 2040. Continuing to rely on them could force the rail sector into higher costs and reduced reliability, as knowledge of these systems declines and critical components become harder to source. Second, the GSM-R (2G) network has to be replaced by FRMCS (5G), but specifications for the new system are not expected until 2029. This situation adds further delays, as the transition requires extensive adjustments to both rolling stock and infrastructure.

Thirdly, the report highlights that the current working method, installing ERTMS in sequential tranches, is too slow and expensive. The first tranche, which began on the Northern lines, Zeeland line, and Kijfhoek-Belgian border section, has already delayed projects originally planned for the Hanzelijn, Schiphol-Amsterdam-Almere-Lelystad railway corridor (SAAL), Brabant route, and Utrecht-Meteren.

To meet the challenge, the ERTMS Programme Directorate is pushing for a more ambitious timeline: a nationwide ERTMS rollout by 2040, requiring significant acceleration from 2030 onwards. The proposed solution is to install ERTMS in parallel across multiple regions, rather than one track section at a time, whenever an opportunity arises.

Whether this approach is feasible depends on several factors. For example, there needs to be greater clarity first regarding ProRail’s capacity and the availability of resources and staff. Furthermore, an accelerated rollout would require politicians to reallocate funds that were originally earmarked for it after 2040. The ERTMS Programme Directorate estimates that around €5 billion of funding would already be needed in the period prior to that, as the work would then be carried out at an earlier stage.

The 24th ERTMS Progress Report of the Directorate concludes that while the first phase of ERTMS rollout, Tranche 1, is advancing, complex technical challenges remain. These include delays in the Central Safety System (CSS) caused by new EU specifications.

Tranche 1 consists of the Northern lines, the Zeeland line, and the Kijfhoek-Belgian border section and involves converting 419 kilometres of track to ERTMS, upgrading approximately 1,150 trains and locomotives, and training around 12,000 railway professionals.

The estimated cost for this first phase is €3.8 billion, against a €3.6 billion budget. This creates a €219 million budget tension (a €56 million increase compared to the previous progress report of October 2025), primarily attributed to insufficient price indexation. Additionally, there is a further financial risk profile of at least €105 million, attributed to cost developments of the CSS and the most recent insights on the planning.

The Dutch State Secretary for Infrastructure, Annet Bertram, will review the findings of the Programme Directorate and respond in the autumn of 2026. Meanwhile, the Directorate is refining its proposal for Tranche 2, which will focus on upgrading the outdated ERTMS systems on the HSL-Zuid, the high-speed line connecting Amsterdam and Rotterdam to Brussels and beyond. This upgrade is intended to be finalised before the current management contract, held by Infraspeed BV, expires on March 31, 2031, after which the Dutch state intends to transfer management to infrastructure manager ProRail.

The existing ERTMS sections in the Netherlands, on the HSL-Zuid, Betuweroute, Amsterdam-Utrecht, and Hanzelijn are equipped with ERTMS Baseline 2 and do not align with the newer systems being installed. These sections will also need upgrades or replacements between 2030 and 2040. Unlike Tranches 1 and 2, Tranche 3 will not be an execution phase for specific rail lines but rather a simultaneous preparatory phase to establish the groundwork and preconditions needed for the accelerated national rollout towards the 2040 ambition.

news.title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
news.title_en: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
news.author: Reed Albergotti
news.content_snippet:
Export controls on chips and other technology shouldn’t aim to cut China off completely — a strategy that will only backfire, warns Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, the sole maker of the lithography machines needed to produce the world’s most advanced AI chips.

“You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don’t completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on devel
news.summary_en: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should target only the most advanced technology rather than a total blockade. He warned that over-restricting China forces domestic acceleration in chip development, whereas maintaining a 'generation gap' via older equipment exports keeps Beijing tethered to Western hardware ecosystems.
paragraphs: Export controls on chips and other technology shouldn’t aim to cut China off completely — a strategy that will only backfire, warns Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, the sole maker of the lithography machines needed to produce the world’s most advanced AI chips.

“You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don’t completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on development,” Fouquet said on Semafor’s Future Proof.

The debate over Chinese access to Western technology has intensified in Washington after revelations of Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy left lawmakers divided on how aggressively to tighten curbs.

As a $520 billion de facto monopoly in chipmaking equipment, ASML sits at the center of that fight. Fouquet argued that continuing to sell China older equipment — ASML’s shipments there are more than a decade behind the cutting edge — maintains a strategic “generation gap” that keeps Beijing hooked on Western hardware rather than racing to build its own.

“For almost 30 years, we have been able to keep an extremely high market share in China — very high means close to 100% — which means that they have accepted to rely on our technology with the idea that they had access to it,” Fouquet said.

news.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
news.title_en: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks

inline_images.caption: ARTEX's architecture splits tasks across specialized AI agents. | Image: Microsoft
inline_images.caption_en: ARTEX's architecture splits tasks across specialized AI agents. | Image: Microsoft

news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.content_snippet:
The AI framework ARTEX automates cyberattacks from reconnaissance to data theft. A Microsoft analysis shows how state-backed groups and cybercriminals use its specialized agents at machine speed, and how defenders can respond.

Since its release in July 2026, the AI-powered penetration-testing framework ARTEX has become a go-to tool for cyberattacks. The software was recently suspected of being used in an intrusion into an analytics system run by the CIA, NGA, and ODNI (Link nicht geprüft). That
news.summary_en: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported that the AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX is being exploited by state-backed groups, including Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon. The framework uses a multi-agent architecture to automate the entire attack lifecycle, significantly lowering the barrier for complex breaches against sensitive infrastructure and agencies.
paragraphs: The AI framework ARTEX automates cyberattacks from reconnaissance to data theft. A Microsoft analysis shows how state-backed groups and cybercriminals use its specialized agents at machine speed, and how defenders can respond.

Since its release in July 2026, the AI-powered penetration-testing framework ARTEX has become a go-to tool for cyberattacks. The software was recently suspected of being used in an intrusion into an analytics system run by the CIA, NGA, and ODNI (Link nicht geprüft). That breach surfaced shortly before US financial crimes agency FinCEN reported a security incident. The FBI and the US Department of Agriculture had reported incidents earlier.

A report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence now details how ARTEX works and how widely it has spread. GitHub user "Autumn-27"published the source code in July and deleted it in October, though other developers still distribute copies. Chinese security firm ThreatBook also sells a commercial Pro version. Microsoft says state-backed groups from China and North Korea have integrated ARTEX into their operations, including Salt Typhoon, Crystal Typhoon, Onyx Sleet, and Storm-0940. Financially motivated cybercriminals also use the system, the company says, with both state-backed and criminal groups deploying it in operations such as supply chain attacks.
### Specialized AI agents run existing security tools with minimal oversight

Microsoft points out that ARTEX doesn't invent new attack techniques. Instead, the framework operates existing security software with almost no human intervention, including tools such as Nmap, Sqlmap, Metasploit, and automated headless browsers. Attackers can connect any large language model, including modified versions without safety guardrails. A built-in pooling feature automatically switches models or API keys on errors or usage limits, making attacks hard for any single AI provider to track.

According to Microsoft, the system is built on a multi-agent architecture. A goal model breaks an attacker's instructions into verifiable subgoals. From there, a planning agent continuously reviews a knowledge graph, a dynamic map of discovered systems and vulnerabilities, to assign short attack tasks. Worker agents carry out those tasks via system commands, including deploying web shells on web servers, reading password files, or hijacking cloud accounts. Each new finding feeds back into the map and prompts the planning agent for the next step until a reporting agent documents all exploited flaws.
### Machine-speed attacks push Microsoft to recommend active deception

Automation cuts defender response times to just a few minutes, the company found. In one case, an AI agent took just five minutes to search for accidentally exposed credentials on GitHub and pull data from Azure Key Vault, a cloud key store. During a Storm-0940 campaign, the company logged more than 151,000 failed login attempts from automated password guessing, peaking at 2,900 per minute. In that same campaign, Microsoft observed some compromised apps granting themselves top administrator privileges.

Conventional rule-based filters often fail against ARTEX because they rely on fixed markers like known IP addresses or the browser identifiers "artex-enrich"and "norma."Agents and their human operators constantly change those markers and reroute blocked traffic through rotating VPNs, proxy servers, or Tor. Even when security teams spot and isolate a breach, that is often not enough. Because ARTEX usually runs two to three attack chains simultaneously, its agents adapt immediately and shift to new network paths at machine speed.

ARTEX still gives itself away with huge bursts of traffic, because the framework doesn't hide its activity by default. Microsoft recommends deception technologies tailored to how AI agents operate, alongside strict access controls, rate limits, and automated real-time isolation for compromised devices.

Honeypots present autonomous agents with attractive but worthless decoy systems to pull traffic away from real targets. Artificial delay loops, known as tarpits, slow down requests and drain an agent's built-in time and compute budget. Fake wins, Microsoft says, are especially effective because ARTEX's goal model looks for verifiable proof of a breach. When a trap returns convincing fake success messages, the AI considers its task complete and stops the attack by itself.

Decoy credentials, called honeytokens, trigger early alerts when agents try to hijack someone else's AI compute. Microsoft's own tests show these deception tactics sharply reduce successful attack traffic against real systems and deliver high-precision data for identifying the attackers behind them.
subheadings: Specialized AI agents run existing security tools with minimal oversight
Machine-speed attacks push Microsoft to recommend active deception

news.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
news.title_en: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.content_snippet:
The US is closing cloud loopholes that give Chinese companies access to AI chips. Nvidia is responding by halting shipments to four countries, while thousands of high-performance processors are looking for new buyers on the secondary market.

Nvidia has told manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The Financial Times reported the halt, citing three people familiar with the matter. It isn't clear whether the paus
news.summary_en: Nvidia has directed partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia in response to tightened US BIS export controls. The move aims to prevent Chinese companies from bypassing sanctions via third-country cloud providers, triggering market volatility for B300 chips and imposing strict end-user compliance reviews for regional data centers.
paragraphs: The US is closing cloud loopholes that give Chinese companies access to AI chips. Nvidia is responding by halting shipments to four countries, while thousands of high-performance processors are looking for new buyers on the secondary market.

Nvidia has told manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The Financial Times reported the halt, citing three people familiar with the matter. It isn't clear whether the pause is only temporary, according to the report.

The move follows tighter US export controls from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security. The rules aim to stop Chinese companies from getting around existing sales bans by renting computing power from foreign cloud providers. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC the goal was to block indirect access, including smuggling through Southeast Asia and remote access via data centers in third countries.
### Thousands of B300 chips hit the market as cloud providers face chaos

The controls are already affecting the hardware market, CNBC reported. Since the announcement, dealers have listed an unusually large number of Nvidia GPUs for sale. Jack Duhamel, president of the AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two other insiders confirmed to CNBC that the surge is a direct result of the new rule. According to the report, sellers are looking for new buyers for hardware, including thousands of B300 chips, one of Nvidia's most advanced models. Those chips were originally intended for data centers with Chinese rental customers.

The rollout has created significant uncertainty in Southeast Asia, the Financial Times reported. Cloud providers have 90 days to apply for a license and prove that no restricted companies are among their end users. One cloud provider executive described the situation to the paper as chaos, saying there was no guidance on how to apply.

The fallout is also hitting major infrastructure projects. Banks have halted about $500 million in loans to Singapore-based cloud provider Aolani, which planned to rent computing power to TikTok parent ByteDance, the Financial Times reported. ByteDance could now pull out of the deal.
subheadings: Thousands of B300 chips hit the market as cloud providers face chaos

Previously unreported details show that efforts by OpenAI and Anthropic to prevent distillation - training models using answers generated by more capable models - have slowed Chinese AI development. The measures put at risk a key advantage that has helped Chinese AI companies challenge their U.S. rivals despite years of export controls: developing competitive models at substantially lower cost.

news.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
news.title_en: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
news.author: Isabella Ward
news.content_snippet:
Meta declined a suggestion from the UK’s financial regulator last week that they joint-test Muse using their sandbox, according to the watchdog’s head of innovation Colin Payne. It comes as regulators across the UK, including the competition and data watchdogs, warned Meta it needs to ensure its AI products comply with UK consumer protection laws.

“It’s another force of attack, agents hitting the streets, most of them coming from the US,” Payne, of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), said Tu
news.summary_en: Meta declined a joint-testing request from Colin Payne, head of innovation at the UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), regarding its Muse AI assistant. The FCA is concerned about potential consumer harm in autonomous financial interactions, particularly as Muse integrates with major British retailers.
paragraphs: Meta declined a suggestion from the UK’s financial regulator last week that they joint-test Muse using their sandbox, according to the watchdog’s head of innovation Colin Payne. It comes as regulators across the UK, including the competition and data watchdogs, warned Meta it needs to ensure its AI products comply with UK consumer protection laws.

“It’s another force of attack, agents hitting the streets, most of them coming from the US,” Payne, of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), said Tuesday in a panel hosted by AI firm Whitespace. “We’ve got a number of entrants into the market. We want to see what they’re going to be doing in the market. I think it’s just reasonable,” he later explained to WIRED. Payne told WIRED the FCA had been hoping the organizations could work together to investigate what interactions might look like between the tool, marketed as a personal assistant, and a normal customer.
His organization has been experimenting with other firms as many, including Amazon, roll out AI shopping assistants, and other agentic tools in the UK.

The FCA especially wants to understand how payments will be made by agents—as multiple British retailers, including grocers Sainsbury’s, Marks & Spencer, and Ocado, department store Debenhams Group, and electronics seller Currys said they’d been working with Meta to smooth Muse’s access to their sites. Payne is concerned about potential unintended consequences of prompts, especially when a user has a low level of understanding of how the AI product works. “If an agent is acting autonomously, we want to make sure it’s in the interest of the consumer,” he says.

Payne did note the testing would have taken time to set up. “Normally you have a long period of time speaking to a firm and then you plan it over a period of weeks or months,” he explained, but Meta only made the FCA aware of its plans last month.
“We’ve engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so,” Meta Spokesperson Matthew Pollard tells WIRED.

More than 10 million users have set up Muse in North America since it was launched in September. British watchdogs say they will be monitoring Muse’s rollout closely as they are bracing for significant uptake on their side of the pond, too, given that many Brits already use Meta’s other products, like Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp. “If it’s going to be equally popular in the UK, we need to be able to see what it’s going to do,” Payne says.

The ICO stressed the importance of users understanding and being able to control how Muse uses their personal data. The Competition and Markets Authority has already made Meta adapt its terms and conditions for UK consumers to say Meta must exercise “reasonable skill and care/professional diligence” when providing Muse, the EU and UK terms say, with the document acknowledging that outputs may still be inaccurate and actions may not be completed as intended.
“If we have concerns, we will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers,” the CMA said in a statement.

Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month.
"Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally," Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns.
The world's richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year.
He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work.

"I recommend holding on to your shares," Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could "be worth about a million times the current global economy" if it "succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun's energy."
"These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them," he said.
In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be "the first of many."
There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau.
The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk's gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion.
SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion.
The company's Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk's ambition to colonize Mars.

paragraphs: Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand.

Davidson, who is taking part in a clinical trial run by the University of Utah, is the ninth person to have this experimental device implanted in his arm. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently.

The hand is part of the bionic LUKE arm, named after Luke Skywalker of Star Wars , who was fitted with a lifelike prosthetic arm after his own was light-sabered off . The arm was developed in the 2000s , initially trialed in 2014 , and approved by the FDA that same year. The trial that Davidson is enrolled in isn’t so focused on the arm itself but on a new way to connect it to a person’s nervous system. The connection allows users to control movements and receive feedback about how much pressure they’re applying.

Researchers hope that Davidson’s experiences will help them answer some long-standing questions about the technology, including how useful it really is in day-to-day life. They want to know when the device is helpful and where it might fail. They also want to learn how it might affect Davidson’s well-being as well as his brain and nervous system.

In 2009, when he was 16, Davidson climbed a telephone pole to get the best shot of a sunset. “I climbed about 35 feet up,” he recalls. But he lost his footing as he tried to descend. He grabbed for a wire, which ended up electrocuting him, before he fell to the ground.

The accident resulted in second- and third-degree burns over 37% of his body, says Davidson, “and I broke my back in approximately 50 separate locations.” He also broke eight ribs, and his spinal cord was severed. He’s pretty sure he broke his left wrist, too. But around 10 days later, his left hand—his dominant hand, and the one he’d grabbed the wire with—had started to develop gangrene. It was amputated.

Davidson was ultimately in a coma for around a month. “Once I woke up, they explained to me: You’re paralyzed, you’re never going to walk again, and also, we took your left hand,” he recalls. “A bit of an inconvenience at 16, to say the least.”

Davidson, now 33 and a trauma therapist, went on to have physical therapy and adjusted to life in his changed body. He’s tried a range of prosthetic hands. The first one, which he received a year and a half after his injury, was a basic hook that allowed him to pick things up. It wasn’t fancy, but it gave him “a psychological feeling of returning to being whole,” he says.

The hands he’s tried since have been more advanced—some have allowed him to control individual fingers with muscle movements, for example. Some have been covered by his medical insurance, which allows for replacements around every five years, he says. Others he’s had to buy himself. He bought his third prosthetic hand, for example, from eBay. “It’s funny to think I bought a secondhand second hand,” he says.

A chance encounter with a scientist at a supermarket introduced Davidson to the research team at the University of Utah, which specialized in researching devices that plug into the body. Since 2013, the team had been running a trial of a system that could connect with the nerves of a residual limb, allowing an amputee to control a bionic one. Davidson turned out to be an ideal candidate, says Jake George, director of the university’s neurorobotics lab .

Davidson, who was keen to take part, first had to undergo what George describes as “pretty extensive” physical and psychological evaluations. Not only did he have to be well enough for surgery, but the team also scanned his brain to make sure that he still had a mental representation of his left hand—suggesting he’d be able to move a bionic one. They also ran tests to check that the nerves in his arm were working.

A therapist evaluated Davidson’s motivations for taking part in the trial. “Our patients aren’t being compensated, they don’t get to keep the device, and they go through two surgeries—the surgery to get it in and the surgery to take it out,” says George. “Avi’s doing this because he wants to help others.”

news.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
news.title_en: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
news.author: Terrence O'Brien
news.summary_en:
A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off “the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts — more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors — with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold.”

In October, Character.AI filed for bankrupt
paragraphs: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off “the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts — more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors — with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold.”

In October, Character.AI filed for bankruptcy following years of scandals and legal challenges, including from Disney. Disney ended up buying some of the company’s assets and hiring its CEO, Karandeep Anand, in a sort of “acquihire” arrangement that will also see “a number of Character.AI’s technical team” join the entertainment giant. The Disney deal also faced opposition from a similarly broad coalition of AGs.

The main point of contention with Character.AI’s plan to sell its chat data is that it offers no protections for users. The AGs say there are no requirements that the buyer honor existing privacy policies, no avenues for users to delete their data, and no inherent limits on what a buyer could do with that data, including selling it on to yet another party. It doesn’t help that the first bidder has a limited paper trail, having only been established on November 13th, 2026, with no parent company or investors listed.

Some states, including New York, Connecticut, California, and Colorado, have also passed laws regulating chatbots that Character.AI may be in violation of when they go into effect on January 1st, 2027.

news.summary_en: Dragos Chief Research Officer HD Moore revealed that AI startup MiniMax improperly stores private web links from user prompts despite opt-out requests. Security researchers observed unauthorized third-party access to these links, accompanied by suspicious traffic originating from Beijing, Shanghai, and the Moscow region, alongside attempts to exfiltrate private software code.
paragraphs: Confidential data sent to Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup MiniMax (0100.HK) was accessed by unidentified third parties, it has emerged. The finding was disclosed by HD Moore, chief research officer (CRO) of US cybersecurity firm Dragos, who said the access occurred even when users specified they did not want their data stored or retained.

In a blog post dated the 19th of this month, Dragos published research findings showing that private web links embedded in requests to AI services were later opened by unauthorized third parties. The company's name was withheld at that time, but Moore has now confirmed that the company in question was MiniMax. This is the first time Dragos has named MiniMax, and the first time Russia-related findings from the investigation have been reported.

According to Moore, one secret link sent to MiniMax surfaced weeks later in a chat channel on Feishu, the workplace messaging app developed by China's ByteDance, and was opened from devices in Beijing and Shanghai. Researchers also detected suspicious internet traffic from the Moscow region in connection with links sent to MiniMax. However, no evidence has been confirmed proving that the links were actually opened from Russia.

Between July and November, Dragos sent roughly 2 million requests containing secret web links and test login credentials to multiple AI providers, then monitored whether third parties attempted to access those links. According to Moore, links sent through different providers were repeatedly opened two to three days later from internet connections in Singapore, even when users had specified they did not want their information stored. This pattern appeared only when requests were forwarded to MiniMax's cloud, and was not observed when other companies ran the company's models independently.

The research team also detected attempts to download a set of private software code referenced in MiniMax requests. According to Moore, this new activity was observed after access to the secret links appeared to stop around October 22. It is unclear who initiated the attempts or whether the code was actually obtained.
MiniMax listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange this year. The company develops multimodal AI models capable of processing multiple types of data, as well as consumer apps.

In response to the reports, MiniMax said in a statement dated the 25th that its security systems had collected and stored web links contained in messages sent to its AI models through other service providers. The systems automatically opened some links in order to check for potential security threats, it said.

The company said it did not retain entire conversations and that the stored addresses have been deleted. It added that these activities have been halted and that no evidence was found in the requests it examined that customer conversations or AI responses were disclosed to third parties.

Atlas Cloud, a US AI service provider that offers access to MiniMax's models, is one of the companies affected by the data leak. According to a spokesperson, the company had adopted a policy of using MiniMax's data center in Singapore to avoid having customer data processed in China. However, information sent through its platform may have leaked after reaching MiniMax, the spokesperson said.

Atlas Cloud has stopped forwarding requests to MiniMax and has warned customers who used the M3, M2.7, and M3.1 Flash models that confidential information they sent may have leaked. The company also said MiniMax's explanation is consistent with its own investigation findings.

AI platform OpenRouter has also removed three providers, tightened its data privacy requirements, and notified potentially affected customers. It said no evidence has been confirmed that its systems were compromised.

The findings raise questions about the safety of sensitive software, financial records, and customer information as Chinese-made AI models gain users worldwide on the strength of low prices and improving performance. In October, Chinese-made models occupied the top three spots on AI platform OpenRouter by volume of text processed. In the United States, there is also a move to consider requiring American companies to disclose their use of Chinese-made AI.

news.content_snippet:
Tech experts are warning that a global memory chip shortage driven by technology giants is causing prices to soar for many consumer electronic products.

“All these AI data centres that are powering all these AI tools, they need huge amounts of RAM and they are basically gobbling it up right now,” said Mike Agerbo from GetConnected Media.

news.summary_en: Global memory chip supplies are tightening as tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Meta aggressively procure RAM for AI data center expansion. This shift has triggered a surge in consumer electronic manufacturing costs, with industry experts projecting significant retail price hikes and supply constraints lasting through 2027.

“The sentiment on semis is now exactly the sentiment we had on
news.summary_en: Investors are rotating away from semiconductor dominance toward software firms possessing proprietary datasets and entrenched customer bases. Despite early 2026 sell-offs driven by fears of AI-driven obsolescence, the software sector now exhibits greater defensive value amidst broader tech market volatility.
paragraphs: Semiconductor and software stocks are neck-and-neck in market performance so far this year following a sharp turnaround in sentiment about the winners and losers of the AI boom, as a bruising tech sell-off upends this year’s popular trades.
Software shares have been relatively unscathed by this month’s brutal rout in the tech sector, which has been concentrated in the semiconductor stocks that until recently were investor darlings.
“The sentiment on semis is now exactly the sentiment we had on software six to nine months ago,” said Max Uleer, head of cross-asset strategy at Deutsche Bank.

Investors dumped the stocks of software companies earlier this year on fears that advances in AI technology would undermine their business models. But the sector reversed those losses in the second half of the year and has held on to its gains in the recent volatility, highlighting a shift in how investors are thinking about the market impact of the AI revolution.

“Undeniably, the narrative has moved for software as a sector, which was perceived as universally challenging, into a defined group of those who will be the structural winners and those who will not,” said Lawrence Jamieson, co-head of Emea equity capital markets at Barclays.
Kristina Hooper, chief market strategist at Man Group, said: “The view from 40,000 feet is that markets don’t know who the winners and losers [from AI] will ultimately be.”
She said 2026 had been “a guessing game, where investors have made somewhat snap judgments, like the assumption that software firms and their products would become obsolete”.
“The thinking has evolved over time to questioning that thesis and ultimately worrying about semiconductors,” she added.
The software and semiconductor sub-indices of the S&P 500 are now both marginally negative year-to-date, with software stocks outperforming semiconductors.

The software sell-off at the start of 2026 gathered speed after the release of new tools by AI lab Anthropic, which gave users the ability to more easily perform complex legal, sales and marketing functions.
As the sell-off deepened, being overweight semiconductor stocks compared to benchmarks while being underweight software stocks became a hedge fund favourite trade earlier this year.

But the worst of the fears for the software sector have since faded, with investors reassured by the defensive value of companies’ large customer bases and their perceived “moats” of proprietary data sets.

news.title_en: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
news.author: Zijing Wu
news.content_snippet:
Nvidia has told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to four south-east Asian countries, as the US steps up export controls to prevent Chinese access to AI computing power.

Manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro, which package Nvidia’s chips into servers, have told buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that Nvidia will not allow their orders to be shipped, according to three people with knowledge of the matter.

It is unclear whether the halt is tempor
news.summary_en: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia to comply with new US export control regulations. This measure targets the loophole allowing Chinese AI developers to access restricted high-end GPU compute via local cloud providers, as firms struggle with the lack of specific compliance guidelines.
paragraphs: Nvidia has told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to four south-east Asian countries, as the US steps up export controls to prevent Chinese access to AI computing power.

Manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro, which package Nvidia’s chips into servers, have told buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that Nvidia will not allow their orders to be shipped, according to three people with knowledge of the matter.
It is unclear whether the halt is temporary, as Nvidia and its partners try to work out how to comply with Washington’s new export controls, the people said.
The four south-east Asian countries have become favoured destinations for Chinese AI developers seeking to access Nvidia’s most advanced chips, whose exports are restricted by Washington.

The region is lucrative for Nvidia. The chipmaker booked $104bn of revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, a 72 per cent increase in 12 months, according to company accounts. Nvidia also records some of its Taiwan and China revenue via its Singapore unit.
Many Chinese groups get around US export controls by renting access through cloud computing providers that buy servers containing Nvidia chips.

The US commerce department introduced new rules last week aimed at stopping the practice. The measures came after Jensen Huang was briefly ousted as chief executive of Nvidia following reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman tied to a cloud provider that leased access to Chinese companies and is being investigated for alleged involvement in smuggling.
The revelations complicated Huang’s stance that the US should continue selling Nvidia chips to Chinese companies to increase their dependence on American technology.

Despite Beijing’s push to develop domestic alternatives, China’s leading AI labs remain heavily reliant on Nvidia’s processors to develop their flagship models, particularly during compute-intensive early-stage training.

While many were hoping Huang’s return to the helm of Nvidia this week would open a path to less strict enforcement of the new rules, there is little indication that the company will hold back from executing them, said the people.
The commerce department has set a 90-day deadline for cloud providers to obtain a licence by proving that their end users do not include restricted entities.

“There’s this new rule but no guidance on execution,” said an executive at a cloud provider. “No one knows how to apply for this licence while the 90-day clock is ticking. It’s causing sheer chaos in the region.”

paragraphs: Shein Global Holdings Ltd.’s return to India through a local partner is off to a slow start, due to supply chain snags, leadership uncertainty and a lack of proprietary technology that made the fast-fashion brand a hit. It relaunched in February 2025, hoping to ride the retail might of Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries Ltd., but the venture has struggled to regain its former glory, people familiar with the matter said, speaking on condition of anonymity about private matters.

User adoption remains weak: the app averaged about 6 million monthly active users in October, down from the previous month and broadly unchanged from January levels, according to estimates shared by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. By comparison, market leader Myntra, an indirect unit of Walmart Inc., averaged about 100 million monthly active users.

These metrics are a far cry from Shein’s 2017 debut in the country, when it drew hordes of customers looking for trendy clothes and pocket-friendly prices. It was then among dozens of Chinese apps, including TikTok, that New Delhi banned in 2020 over security concerns. Before the ban, India accounted for 67% of Shein’s monthly active users in 2019, according to Sensor Tower.

The tepid restart is a challenge for Isha Ambani, the Ambani scion who oversees the conglomerate’s consumer business. Reliance Retail’s stable includes partnerships with a gamut of global brands like Marks & Spencer, Pret A Manger, Hamleys and Sephora, a broad range that risks causing the enterprise to sag under its own weight.

For Shein, the underwhelming India partnership means it cannot lean on the world’s most populous nation for growth as it battles weak demand in Europe and the US, its two biggest markets. Challenges ahead Reliance is in charge of all operations in India, including product selection, marketing and sales, the people said.

As a result, Shein has not shared its proprietary technology that allows the Chinese giant to spot, design and produce new styles in less than 10 days. Reliance has thus had to build critical processes — from vendor on-boarding to production workflows — from scratch, the people said.

Reliance also lacks Shein’s vast manufacturing network in China. It has tapped smaller Indian makers to produce the apparel instead, many of which are not accustomed to producing the Gen-Z focused styles the brand is known for. Suppliers have had to adjust to unusually specific requirements, resulting in additional training, higher wastage, and longer turnaround times, people familiar said.

Employees have also had to compete internally for funds and management attention, given Reliance Retail’s sprawling collection of businesses and rapidly expanding brand portfolio. Early leadership churn added to the uncertainty. Former Meta Platforms Inc. executive Manish Chopra, who was helping Reliance set up the Shein venture, left the group in 2024 within a year of joining, according to his LinkedIn profile.
Shein and Reliance Retail did not respond to queries from Bloomberg News. Chopra declined to comment. The broader market has also shifted.

India’s online fashion and lifestyle segment — projected to reach $45 billion by 2028 — has become crowded during Shein’s absence. Myntra, Tata Group’s Trent Ltd., Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd. and upstarts like Meesho Ltd. have broadened their appeal among India’s price-sensitive consumers.

“Shein is reentering a market that is already incredibly competitive,” Kara Lee, senior insights analyst at Sensor Tower said. “There’s just a stronger natural consumer preference toward brands that have been able to exist in that space this entire time.” Consumer engagement reflects that pivot.

Shein users in India spent about four minutes a week on the app over the past two months, below the global average of 6.6 minutes, according to Sensor Tower estimates. Download trends paint an even bleaker picture: despite a 60% year-on-year increase in advertising spending in September, downloads fell 73% from a year earlier to 790,000.

news.summary_en: Situational Awareness, a hedge fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, reported a 65% net loss for Q3 following a liquidity crisis triggered by aggressive leveraged bets on the AI sector in July. The fund, which was forced to sell a significant portion of its public equity portfolio to Citadel to stave off implosion, is now pivoting toward more conservative risk management.
paragraphs: Leopold Aschenbrenner, whose Situational Awareness hedge fund nearly unraveled over the summer after its borrowing-fueled bets on artificial intelligence soured, told investors it lost 65% after fees in the third quarter as it worked to learn from its mistakes.

The fund is up 88.5% after fees for the year through September, Aschenbrenner said in an investor letter seen by The Wall Street Journal, telling clients that investing opportunities today “are the highest potential return we have seen in the lifetime of the fund.”

(Bloomberg) -- Situational Awareness told investors it lost 65% after fees in the third quarter, after highly levered bets on artificial intelligence firms nearly led to the hedge fund’s implosion in July, according to the Wall Street Journal.

The hedge fund is still up 88.5% after fees for the year through the month of September, founder Leopold Aschenbrenner said in a letter viewed by the Wall Street Journal. Despite the tumult, the fund stills sees opportunities to invest with high potential for return, according to the report.

Situational Awareness was pushed to the brink in July as a brief moment of panic about AI spread across global markets, sparking margin calls from banks and turning it into a symbol of the wild swings that have accompanied the AI trade. The firm ultimately sold a large chunk of its public equities portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel.

Aschenbrenner, who named his firm after a viral essay he wrote in 2024, has focused on firms he thinks will benefit from the AI revolution. He quickly became known for using leverage to ramp up his returns and his risks.

Aschenbrenner said in the letter that he was taking a more measured approach to risk management, having learned a lesson from the recent turmoil. “Volatility, yes; existential risk, even if we are totally wrong, never,” he reportedly told investors.

The third quarter performance referenced in the letter does not capture the more recent selloff in the market during the month of October, when valuations of AI companies came under scrutiny and wild swings in stocks tied to the artificial intelligence buildout have made it an even more complicated market for investors to navigate.

Aschenbrenner wrote in the letter that Situational Awareness’s portfolio was composed of about 70% publicly traded stocks and 30% positions in private companies following the IPO of Anthropic, its largest private position, according to the report. The firm may rebalance its portfolio away from Anthropic, though it’s “highly bullish” at the IPO price, the WSJ reported.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Great paper from Microsoft on how much coding agents over-edit.

It is widely assumed that coding agents over-edit, because their patches are larger than developer patches.

This study tested that claim on 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories from 18 frontier models. Their method, Delta Residue Attribution, reverts each block of the final patch, reruns the task tests, and records whether the block was needed.

On SWE-bench Verified, most of the extra lines are tests (61%) and documentation (13%). Agent code was on average at least as necessary as developer code (0.887 vs 0.864), and 11 of 18 models left less unneeded code than developers.

About 11% of an agent's code units were still unneeded, and 89% of those changed behavior. Code necessity had no relation to resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified and a negative one on DeepSWE (Spearman -0.59).

Pruning with only the tests the agent can see removed most of the unneeded code, and 89% of pruned patches still resolved the task.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34875

Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/how-much-do-coding-agents-over-edit-and-why-an-empirical-study-of-unneeded-edits-2611.34875

人们普遍认为编码代理会过度编辑，因为他们的补丁比开发人员补丁大。

这项研究在 18 个前沿模型的 7,660 个已解析的 GitHub Copilot CLI 轨迹上测试了这一说法。他们的方法，Delta Residue Attribution，恢复最终补丁的每个块，重新运行任务测试，并记录是否需要该块。

在 SWE-bench Verified 上，大多数额外行是测试 (61%) 和文档 (13%)。平均而言，代理代码至少与开发人员代码一样必要（0.887 vs 0.864），并且 18 个模型中有 11 个模型留下的不需要的代码少于开发人员。

大约 11% 的代理代码单元仍然不需要，其中 89% 的行为发生了变化。代码必要性与 SWE-bench Verified 上的解析率无关，而 DeepSWE 上的解析率为负值 (Spearman -0.59)。

仅使用代理可以看到的测试进行修剪，删除了大部分不需要的代码，并且 89% 的修剪补丁仍然解决了任务。

celebrity.title_zh:
预注册 P = 的更新NP。
欢迎不同意见、更正和辩论。

1. 如果P=NP，则常数为银河常数；否则世界将会变得非常不同。
1a.这意味着数学从根本上来说比预期的更难理解，并且表明我们不会看到“好的”数学对齐结果。 （抄送：@geoffr
celebrity.author: @davidmanheim
celebrity.summary_zh:
eyirving / @OAvnery）
1b.如果银河常数的说法也是错误的（先验 ≈ ε），我将从根本上重新审视许多关于我们对世界的理解程度的事情，包括 AGI 打破当前已知物理学的可行性。 （另外，再见网络安全，如果这是真的，这甚至不是我最大的担忧，即使这是最直接的担忧。）

2. 如果其他领域/ASI 的进展继续快速推进，但要到 2027 年之后才能有结果，我会有点惊讶。
2a.我已经开始更新（基于缺乏答案）一些从根本上来说更困难的事情，而 ASI 无法做对我们来说基本上很神奇的事情。
2b.无论我们是否得到结果，或者得到哪个答案，都不会实质性地改变我对平淡对齐的可能性的看法——这对我来说非常不清楚，如果我们不停止的话，这也是最重要的问题。

3. 如果 P != NP，我的 ASI 时间表会变得更紧。
3a.如果我们在 2027 年中期之前找到答案，那么剩下的不确定性主要与机器人技术的进展有关；条件是到那时还不会加速，ASI 的时间表可能约为 2028 年。
3b.如果我们发现 2027 年末，请参见 2，但稍微不那么极端。

4. 我强烈希望任何非建设性的证明都不会简单到人们能够理解，至少在最初是这样。
4a.如果人工智能开始产生*简单的*证明，例如数学家所说的那些“来自书本”，对于在此之前的任何其他重要证明，我会重新审视这一点。
4b.如果有一个 LEAN 验证器证明 P=NP，但它不是建设性的并且数学家不理解它，那么这只是轻微的边缘证据，表明 LEAN 的依赖类型理论是靠不住的，并且改变了我对许多其他事情的信心。

（更暂定：）
5. 如果 P ?=NP 被证明与我们的公理无关，我期望得出结论，我们应该在实践中接受/使用更强的公理。例如如果 P!=NP 仅当广义连续统假设，或者选择公理，或者相反，我们应该将其视为强有力的证据，甚至是宇宙以这种方式运行的事实证明 - 抄送：@shaibendavid5 和 @HaleviShai

注意：我不是数学家，我是一位超级预测家和具有一定数学背景的人工智能/技术政策专家。我希望能够确信我对上述从属权利要求中至少一项存在重大错误。
celebrity.full_text_en:
Preregistering updates for P =? NP.
Disagreements, corrections, and debate are welcome.

1. If P=NP, the constants will be galactic; the world would look very different otherwise.
1a. This implies math is fundamentally much less understandable than expected, and suggests that we won't see "nice" mathematical alignment results. (cc: @geoffreyirving / @OAvnery)
1b. If the galactic constants claim is also wrong, (prior ≈ ε), I'd be fundamentally revisiting lots of things about how well we understand the world, including the feasibility of AGI breaking currently known physics. (Also, goodbye cybersecurity, which is not even my biggest worry if this is true, even if it's the most immediate one.)

2. If progress on other areas / towards ASI continues apace, but there are no results until after 2027, I will be slightly surprised.
2a. I would already have started updating (based on the lack of an answer) about some things being fundamentally harder, and ASI not being able to do things that are basically magic to us.
2b. Whether or not we get a result, or which answer obtains, does not materially change my views about likelihood of prosaic alignment - which is deeply unclear to me, and the most important question if we don't stop.

3. If P != NP, my timelines for ASI become somewhat tighter.
3a. If we find out before mid-2027, remaining uncertainty is largely about robotics progress; conditional on that not also accelerating by then, timelines are likely ~2028 for ASI.
3b. If we find out late 2027, see 2, but slightly less extreme.

4. I strongly expect any non-constructive proof will not be simple enough for people to understand, at least initially.
4a. If AI starts to produce *simple* proofs, e.g. those which mathematicians say are 'from the book', for any other significant proofs before this, I'd revisit this.
4b. If there is a LEAN verifier that P=NP, but it's not constructive and mathematicians don't understand it, it's slight marginal evidence that LEAN's dependent type theory is wonky, and changes my confidence in lots of other things.

(More tentatively:)
5.  If P ?=NP is proved to be independent of our axioms, I expect to conclude we should be accepting / using stronger axioms in practice. e.g. if P!=NP only if Generalized Continuum Hypothesis, or if Axiom of Choice, or the reverse, we should treat this as stong evidence or even de-facto proof that the universe works that way - cc: @shaibendavid5  & @HaleviShai  

Note: I am not a mathematician, I'm a superforecaster and AI / tech policy wonk with some background in math. I expect to be convinced I'm materially wrong about at least 1 of the above subclaims.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Terence Tao on reading a hard proof with AI

"If you start with a much more complicated argument, I would not just one-shot the proof. That doesn't teach you much of anything."

"If there's a result which is true in all dimensions, ask the AI: can you simplify the argument to only do the one-dimensional case, and just remove all parts of the argument that don't have to do with high dimensions? You might get a simpler document that you try to understand first.?

"A lot of this you should be doing at a whiteboard or blackboard with pen and paper. These tools are useful for cleaning everything up, and if there is some nasty computation where you don't care to understand exactly how the signs work, you just need to know the answer, you can use these tools, but also knowing when not to use them is part of the challenge."

圆周率
🟢爱马仕代理

查看 SWE-bench Pro 上的 OpenCode（最难的 51 项任务），启用思考：
🧠 原版 Qwen3.8-27B → 47.1%
🔥 配备超级适配器 → 66.7% 👈

两个版本解决的任务上的工具调用减少了 31%。

在所有六种安全带/基准组合中，Hugging Face 报告：

🔥 平均通过@1 → 55.5% 至 63.5%
🔥 启用思考后工具调用减少 19–48%

怎么办？他们采用了三个单独的 RL 训练 LoRA，并将它们的权重更新合并到一个 96 级适配器中。

合并不需要额外的培训。
💾 适配器 → ~956MB
🧠 基础型号 → Qwen3.8-27B
🔓 阿帕奇 2.0
💻 GGUF 可用于 llama.cpp

一个重要的区别。在我最初的 OpenCode 帖子中，用 Think Off 测量了专业适配器。这些新的超级适配器结果使用了思维ON。

基准测试是 Hugging Face 自己的 BF16 评估，未经过验证的 llama.cpp 性能。

该团队现在发布了一个单独的思维优化 Pi 适配器，报告称共享解决任务中生成的令牌大约减少了 35-42%。
